points: Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria and did evil, following the sins of Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: The anger of the Most High was kindled and He delivered Israel into the hand of Hazael and Ben-hadad of Syria all their days.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Jehoahaz besought the Most High, who heard him and gave Israel a saviour so they escaped the hand of the Syrians, yet they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Jehoahaz was left with only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, for Syria had destroyed the rest and made them like dust.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Jehoahaz slept with his fathers and Joash his son reigned in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Joash also did evil and departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, and he fought against Amaziah king of Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Elisha fell sick of the sickness he would die of, and Joash king of Israel came and wept over him, calling him the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Elisha had the king take bow and arrows, laid his own hands on the king's hands, and had him shoot eastward as the arrow of the Lord's deliverance from Syria.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Then Elisha told him to smite the ground, and the king smote only three times and stopped; Elisha was angry, saying he should have smitten five or six times to consume Syria, but now would smite Syria only three times.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Elisha died and was buried, and when a dead man was cast into his sepulchre and touched his bones, the man revived and stood on his feet.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz, but the Most High was gracious and had compassion because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: After Hazael died, Jehoash beat Ben-hadad his son three times and recovered the cities of Israel, according to the word Elisha spoke.
